claim: Independently-generated LLM code implementations fail on the same test cases far more often than chance/independence would predict, violating the N-Version Programming failure-independence assumption.
stance_target: correlated (non-independent) failure structure across LLM-generated code solutions
scope_conditions: 224 problems x 12 models x 5 languages x 3 prompting strategies
quoted_support: implementations from different models showing higher diversity yet still failing on the same tests far more often than expected under independence.

claim: N-version ensembles of LLM-generated code realize only a fraction of the reliability gain achievable under true failure independence, and this fraction drops further when ensemble members come from the same model.
stance_target: practical cost of correlated failures for ensemble/voting-based code reliability
quoted_support: three- and five-version ensembles realize only 0.43 and 0.44 of the reliability gain achievable under independence, dropping below 0.3 when ensembles are built from the same model.

claim: Manual fault analysis shows that even implementations with different observable failure patterns often share the same underlying root cause.
stance_target: shared latent failure mechanisms underlying superficially distinct code errors
scope_conditions: manual inspection subset of the 224-problem corpus
quoted_support: Manual fault analysis shows that even different failure patterns often share root causes.
